I have already contributed the package recipe to zeroclaw upstream, and @commandodev has contributed the package independently to llm-agents.nix

I also had a PR open to add a nixos module, which I closed in favor of getting it into nixpkgs:
zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#2955

I had to add a patch for the AutonomyConfig, otherwise one needs to specify every single field of it, even though one only wants to change one.

Since there are many different configuration settings, I think it's not feasible to replicate everything as a nixos option. What is most critical are any secrets. So secrets can be specified with options.

Summary

Telemt - MTProxy for Telegram on Rust + Tokio.

This PR:

  1. Adds me as a maintainer
  2. Adds the missing custom license
  3. Introduces a NixOS module for telemt with a systemd service

Changes

  • maintainers/maintainer-list.nix: Added me
  • pkgs/by-name/te/telemt/package.nix: Added meta.license
  • nixos/modules/services/networking/telemt.nix: New module
  • nixos/modules/module-list.nix: Registered the new module

Motivation

The package alone isn't useful without a systemd service to run telemt as a system service.

The NixOS module provides:

  • Automatic systemd service setup
  • Mutually exclusive declarative settings and imperative configFile options
  • Option to automatically open the firewall port for service
  • Proper sandboxing via systemd hardening options

Testing

Manually verified:

  • Package builds: nix-build -A telemt
  • Declarative settings generates config and the service runs
  • Imperative configFile uses the provided file and the service runs
  • Assertion fires when the module is misconfigured

cc @r4v3n6101 (original package author)

items.content_html:
Description

Add a new NixOS module for synchronizing kernel patches from lore.kernel.org.

Features

  • Periodic sync from kernel mailing list archives via public-inbox
  • Support for 14 kernel subsystems:
    • dri-devel - DRM/Graphics
    • netdev - Networking
    • linux-fsdevel - Filesystems
    • linux-mm - Memory management
    • linux-security-module - LSM
    • linux-hardening - KSPP hardening
    • rust-for-linux - Rust kernel development
    • linux-block, linux-btrfs, linux-ext4, linux-xfs - Storage
    • linux-usb, linux-pci - Hardware
  • Optional public-inbox/lei support for full mbox archives
  • Fallback to Atom feeds for lightweight sync
  • Automatic index generation
  • Full systemd hardening (DynamicUser, sandboxing)

Motivation

Kernel developers and security teams need to track upstream patch discussions. This module provides an automated way to sync patches from lore.kernel.org, the official Linux kernel mailing list archive.

Example Usage

Basic setup:

services.lore-sync = {
  enable = true;
  subsystems = [ "linux-hardening" "rust-for-linux" ];
};

Full configuration:

services.lore-sync = {
  enable = true;
  subsystems = [ "dri-devel" "netdev" "rust-for-linux" ];
  interval = "6h";
  lookbackDays = 14;
  useLei = true;  # Use public-inbox for full mbox
};

Use Cases

  • Kernel developers tracking patch discussions
  • Security teams monitoring hardening patches (KSPP)
  • Anyone following Rust-for-Linux development
  • Maintainers tracking filesystem/driver patches

Checklist

  • Module follows nixpkgs conventions
  • Options have descriptions and examples
  • systemd service is hardened (DynamicUser, sandboxing)
  • Added to nixos/modules/module-list.nix
  • Documentation (can add if requested)
  • NixOS test (can add if requested)

Related

  • lore.kernel.org: https://lore.kernel.org/
  • public-inbox: https://public-inbox.org/

items.content_html:
Description

Add a new NixOS module for automated CVE synchronization from the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).

Features

  • Periodic CVE data fetching from NVD API 2.0
  • Incremental sync with state tracking (only fetches modified CVEs)
  • CPE-based product filtering (e.g., filter for Linux kernel CVEs only)
  • Automatic kernel CVE extraction for security monitoring
  • Full systemd hardening (DynamicUser, sandboxing, restricted syscalls)
  • Optional API key support for higher rate limits

Motivation

Security-conscious NixOS users and organizations need visibility into CVEs affecting their systems. This module provides the foundation for CVE awareness by fetching authoritative data directly from NIST NVD.

Example Usage

Basic setup:
```nix
services.nvd-sync = {
enable = true;
extractKernelCves = true;
};
```

With API key:
```nix
services.nvd-sync = {
enable = true;
apiKeyFile = config.sops.secrets.nvd-api-key.path;
interval = "hourly";
products = [ "cpe:2.3:o:linux:linux_kernel" ];
};
```

Checklist

  • Module follows nixpkgs conventions
  • Options have descriptions and examples
  • systemd service is hardened (DynamicUser, sandboxing)
  • Added to nixos/modules/module-list.nix
  • Documentation (can add if requested)
  • NixOS test (can add if requested)

items.content_html:
This PR adds a new nixos module for the Antigravity code editor.

The module closely follows the existing programs.vscode module and provides the following functionality:

  • programs.antigravity.enable
  • programs.antigravity.defaultEditor
  • programs.antigravity.package
  • programs.antigravity.extensions
  • programs.antigravity.finalPackage

It uses vscode-with-extensions.override to customize the Antigravity package with extensions, mirroring the behavior of the VS Code module. This allows users to declaratively install extensions and optionally set Antigravity as the default editor.

Example configuration

This enables the application, sets it as the default editor and installs the pkgs.vscode-extensions.bbenoist.nix VScode plugin.

{
  programs.antigravity = {
    enable = true;
    defaultEditor = true;
    extensions = with pkgs.vscode-extensions; [
      bbenoist.nix
    ];
  };
}

items.content_html:
Add a structured alternative to containerdConfigTemplate that accepts Nix attribute sets and generates TOML containerd config. The base template directive ({{ template "base" . }}) is automatically included. This option is mutually exclusive with the existing containerdConfigTemplate string option.

Example usage:

services.k3s.extraContainerdSettings = {
  plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".containerd.runtimes."custom" = {
    runtime_type = "io.containerd.runc.v2";
  };
  plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".containerd.runtimes."custom".options = {
    BinaryName = "/path/to/custom-container-runtime";
  };
};

Depends on #503612 (nixos/rancher: fix warnings/assertions being silently dropped).
